title: Beach walk distance

payload.instruction: Tap the sentence in the AI summary that gets the original wrong.

The beach is about a thirty-minute walk away via a marked trail.
Pets and smoking are not allowed, and there is parking for two cars.

explanation: The listing says the beach is a ten-minute walk, but the summary stretched it to thirty. AI summaries most often slip on numbers, so always re-check any figure against the original before you rely on it.

title: Hotel review

payload.intro: One of these two hotel reviews was written by a person. The other is AI.
payload.instruction: Pick the one written by the human.

options.text: Nestled in the heart of downtown, this hotel offers the perfect blend of comfort, convenience, and charm. The rooms are spacious and inviting, the staff is friendly and attentive, and the amenities are truly top-notch. Whether you are traveling for business or pleasure, this property delivers a seamless experience from check-in to check-out. explanation: The human review names a room number, a front-desk employee, and a weird true detail about the elevator. The AI review is all adjectives in threes — comfort, convenience, and charm — with words like nestled, seamless, and vibrant but zero specifics. Concrete, checkable details are the strongest sign of a real reviewer.

title: Cookie count

payload.source: This oatmeal cookie recipe makes 24 cookies. Cream the butter with brown sugar, then mix in the dry ingredients. Chill the dough for one hour before baking. Bake at 350 degrees for 12 minutes, until the edges are golden. Store in an airtight container for up to five days.
payload.instruction: Tap the sentence in the AI summary that gets the original wrong.

The recipe makes a dozen cookies.
Bake at 350 degrees for 12 minutes until the edges turn golden.
Finished cookies keep in an airtight container for up to five days.

explanation: The recipe makes 24 cookies, but the summary cut it to a dozen. Quantities are one of the most common things AI gets wrong when condensing text — double-check yields and amounts before you shop or bake.

The AI review runs on triads (sleek, durable, impressive) and the classic whether-you-are-X-or-Y formula with no lived experience. Real reviewers describe what actually happened to them.

title: Recipe headnote

explanation: The human headnote admits the cake is ugly and sinks every time — real recipe stories include flaws and oddly specific history like margarine from the A&P in 1987. The AI version is pure superlatives (delightful, decadent, crowd-pleasing) that could sit atop any recipe on earth. Imperfection plus specificity signals a real person.

title: Missed-meeting apology

The AI apology is all abstractions — valuable time, any inconvenience, patience and understanding — with no actual reason and no specific fix. A real apology contains the embarrassing details.

You can cancel for free up to 48 hours before arrival.
Self-parking is a flat $25 for the entire stay.

explanation: Parking is $25 per day, not per stay — over three nights that is $75, three times what the summary implies. Per-day versus per-stay is a subtle wording change with a real cost attached, so slow down whenever a summary states a price.

title: Plumber recommendation

payload.intro: One of these two neighborhood-forum plumber recommendations was written by a person. The other is AI.
payload.instruction: Pick the one written by the human.

options.text: Highly recommend Miller Plumbing. They answered on the first call, arrived right on time the next morning, and diagnosed the issue within minutes. The technician clearly explained the repair options and pricing before starting any work, and left the space spotless when finished. From scheduling to cleanup, the entire experience was seamless and stress-free. It is rare to find a service company that is this professional, punctual, and reasonably priced. They have earned a customer for life!

Gus from Miller Plumbing rebuilt the trap under our kitchen sink in about forty minutes and charged $140, which is $80 less than the quote I got from the big outfit with the billboard. Fair warning: he will tell you about his boat the entire time. It is called the Second Mortgage. The sink has been fine for a year now, and honestly I would have him back just for the updates on the boat.

explanation: Post A describes a flawless generic service arc — on time, spotless, seamless, professional-punctual-reasonable — without a name, a price, or a repair detail. Post B names Gus, the exact job, the exact price, and a boat called the Second Mortgage. Real recommendations come with receipts and irrelevant human detail; frictionless perfection is the machine's signature.
